---
title: Theme
description: The @puzzle/theme package owns Puzzle's design tokens, color themes, typography, fonts, and theme scoping.
---

`@puzzle/theme` is the source of truth for Puzzle's visual design. It turns a typed token object into `--puzzle-*` CSS custom properties, loads Google Fonts, resolves light and dark color schemes, and lets you scope a theme to the whole document or a single subtree. All `@puzzle/ui` components consume these CSS custom properties, so a single `Theme` provider styles your entire application.

## Import

```tsx
import { Theme } from "@puzzle/theme";
```

## Quick start

Wrap your application in a single `Theme` at the root. Without any props it applies the default tokens, follows the user's system color scheme, and injects Puzzle's global styles.

```tsx
import { Theme } from "@puzzle/theme";

const App = () => (
  <Theme>
    <YourApp />
  </Theme>
);
```

A customized root theme typically combines a color theme, fonts, and a few token overrides:

```tsx
<Theme
  theme="system"
  colorTheme="cobalt-sky"
  fonts={{
    heading: { family: "Sora" },
    body: { family: "Inter" },
  }}
  tokens={{
    radius: { md: "0.5rem" },
  }}
>
  <YourApp />
</Theme>
```

## What the package provides

| Area | Description | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Theme` provider | Injects token CSS variables, loads fonts, and applies global styles at root or local scope. | [Theme Provider](/docs/theme/theme-provider) |
| Design tokens | Typed token groups for spacing, radius, shadows, elevation, borders, layout, motion, and z-index. | [Design Tokens](/docs/theme/tokens) |
| Colors | Semantic color roles, light/dark color schemes, and built-in color themes. | [Colors](/docs/theme/colors) |
| Typography & fonts | Named typography roles, fluid font sizes, and Google Font loading. | [Typography & Fonts](/docs/theme/typography) |
| Breakpoints | Shared responsive breakpoints for JavaScript and CSS. | [Breakpoints](/docs/theme/breakpoints) |
| Component overrides | Global link and image component overrides for router and framework integration. | [Component Overrides](/docs/theme/components) |

## Exports

```tsx
import {
  Theme,
  GoogleFont,
  createGoogleFontUrl,
  BREAKPOINTS,
} from "@puzzle/theme";

import type {
  ThemeProps,
  ThemeScope,
  ThemeMode,
  ThemeTokens,
  ThemeTokenOverrides,
  ThemeColorSchemeTokens,
  ThemeTypographyRoleTokens,
  ThemeTypographyFontRole,
  TypographyStyle,
  ColorTheme,
  Breakpoint,
  FontRole,
  FontStyle,
  FontDisplay,
  FontConfig,
  ResolvedFontConfig,
  FontStylesheet,
  ThemeFonts,
  ThemeComponents,
  ThemeLinkComponent,
  ThemeLinkComponentConfig,
  ThemeImageComponent,
} from "@puzzle/theme";
```

## How it works

`Theme` resolves the default tokens, the optional `colorTheme`, and your `tokens` overrides into a flat map of `--puzzle-*` CSS custom properties. It renders a `<style>` element that assigns those variables to `:root` (root scope) or to a generated scope attribute (local scope). Static CSS shipped with the package maps the scheme-specific variables—such as `--puzzle-color-scheme-light-primary` and `--puzzle-color-scheme-dark-primary`—onto the semantic variables like `--puzzle-color-primary` based on the active mode, including automatic `prefers-color-scheme` handling in `system` mode.

Every token value is validated before it is written into CSS, so unsafe values and unknown token names throw instead of silently producing broken styles.
